protocol.py: 11 biology problems (2 errors, 7 warnings, 2 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: buffer (well C1 in slot 1)
   line 105:  p20.aspirate(10, buffer_well)
   At line 105 the tip went into buffer (well C1 in slot 1) while it still carried sample 1
   (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4
   (well A4 in slot 1) and 11 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3
   more in slot 2.
   Affected: well C1 in slot 1.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 105 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing

3. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 83:  p20.aspirate(6, polymerase_well)
   At line 83 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 10 more in slot
   1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at
   room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), fwd primer
   (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 13 more sat on a block that was
   never cold; the robot pipetted there 56 times over the run. The person setting up the
   deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2
   and 10 more in slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 10 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [cdabc5df4e83]

4. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 84:  p20.dispense(6, master_mix_well)
   At line 84 the robot put polymerase into well D1 in slot 1. Take well D1 in slot 1: at
   that moment it was dry, and the water came afterwards, at line 97, to make the 126 ul of
   water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is
   meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought
   the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many
   times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star
   activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: well D1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to well D1 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix
   it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [6f51cb7828a2]

   line 96:  p20.aspirate(vol, water_well)
   At line 96 the tip went into water (well C5 in slot 1) while it still carried polymerase

   liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The

8. WARNING MIX-BEFORE-DRAW: Liquid drawn from well D1 in slot 1 before it was mixed: added
at line 97, drawn at line 117
   line 97:  p20.dispense(vol, master_mix_well)
   At line 97 liquid was added to well D1 in slot 1, which already held a different liquid.
   At line 117 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between.
   Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not
   at the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: well D1 in slot 1.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 97: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer,
   or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the
   volume in the well.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Svec et al. 2015: how good is a PCR efficiency estimate
           https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4822216/
   [848ed30bdaa1]

9. WARNING CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2
in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 9 more into well
D1 in slot 1 it was never meant for
   line 117:  p20.aspirate(13, master_mix_well)
   At line 117 the tip touched the liquid in well D1 in slot 1 while it still carried sample
   1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample
   4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 9 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be
   there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid
   was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11
   other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Affected: well D1 in slot 1.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 117. If one tip must serve many wells,
   dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches
   what is already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [637c47add42b]

10. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 117:  p20.aspirate(13, master_mix_well)
   At line 117 the tip touched the liquid in well D1 in slot 1 while it still carried sample
   1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample
   4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the
   master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate.
   A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a
   no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Affected: well D1 in slot 1.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 117, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [e4f4cfcc02e3]

11. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 12 wells of polymerase with a sample
   line 118:  p20.dispense(13, dest_well)
   At line 118 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 2), and 12 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 4 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [ad3c8eef2fd7]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: water (well C5 in slot 1)
findings.explanation: At line 96 the tip went into water (well C5 in slot 1) while it still carried polymerase (well C2 in slot 1), fwd primer (well C3 in slot 1) and rev primer (well C4 in slot 1) from an earlier step. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 96 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: Liquid drawn from well D1 in slot 1 before it was mixed: added at line 97, drawn at line 117
findings.explanation: At line 97 liquid was added to well D1 in slot 1, which already held a different liquid. At line 117 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 97: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the volume in the well.

findings.title: A used tip carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 9 more into well D1 in slot 1 it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 117 the tip touched the liquid in well D1 in slot 1 while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 9 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 117 the tip touched the liquid in well D1 in slot 1 while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 117, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 12 wells of polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 118 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 2), and 12 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
